solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: To have always been in base, contrary to order

definitions.note: in cricket a batter who stays in for the whole innings, never dismissed, has done this

indicators.note: letters put to order are arranged afresh, so the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something has sat in a base for ever, against the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrary' looks like the signal but it is fodder; 'to order' does the rearranging. In cricket, an opening batter who is still not out when the innings ends is said to have done this.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from cricket: an opener still undismissed at the close of the innings has remained in throughout.

clue.text: Play 'Act I' to be cast — that's unusual

indicators.note: a play's roles are cast, but cast also means thrown into a new shape, so the letters are remoulded

explanation.surface: A director decides to stage the first act of a play, which is unconventional.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something out of the ordinary, not typical of its kind.

clue.text: Check broadcaster's rule

indicators.note: a broadcaster speaks over the air, so what follows is heard rather than read

parts.note: to rule a country is to reign

explanation.surface: A regulator scrutinises the policy of a television company.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to hold back or restrain, as a rider pulls on a horse's strap.

clue.text: Grinding teeth, lions having a good time

indicators.note: grinding crushes things up, so the letters of the two words after are pulverised and remade

explanation.surface: Big cats gnash their teeth while enjoying themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is British slang for a night out carousing, from cats roaming the roofs.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: out on a spree of revelry, like tomcats wandering across the rooftops at night.

clue.text: Leaves river on wartime service

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed on another sits above it, so the river comes first

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
the ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the women's branch of the British Army in the Second World War

explanation.surface: Someone takes leave from a river posting during the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' is a plural noun here: at British boarding schools and colleges such a permission lets a pupil go away for a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-friendly sense: formal permissions for absence granted at schools and colleges.

clue.text: Law graduate, joining sailor's plot, spilled the beans

parts.note: a BL is a Bachelor of Law
AB, able seaman, is a sailor
a flower bed is a plot of ground

explanation.surface: A lawyer joins a seaman's scheme and then betrays the secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to let a secret out, telling what should have stayed hidden.

clue.text: Welcome Lions at home and maintain high standards

parts.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, receive them
a family group of lions is called a pride, with the article
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Hosting the touring rugby side at home and keeping things classy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lions are the British and Irish touring rugby team, which helps the sporting surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to be proud of something and so keep it up to a good level of quality.

clue.text: Fix engineers' item

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps
a couple who are an item form a pair

explanation.surface: An army engineer mends a piece of kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to mend something broken.

clue.text: Drink with only one very large group of birds

indicators.note: the drink is spelt with two of the letter, and keeping only one of them means taking one away

parts.note: bevvy is British slang for a drink, especially alcohol

explanation.surface: A huge flock of birds flies past while someone sips a single drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective noun: a flock of quails or larks, and loosely any large group.

clue.text: Imperfect thread dropped in ink gets left out of the loop

indicators.note: one piece dropped in another is placed inside it

parts.note: taken as written, split around the inserted letters

indicators.note: something imperfect is flawed, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A faulty thread falls into the inkwell and someone feels excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ink' looks like scenery but is split open: 'Imperfect' makes THEDAR, and 'dropped in' sets it inside, so the definition is the closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: uninformed, kept unaware of what others know.

clue.text: Maybe take a trip winsome blonde mainly organised

indicators.note: organised letters are put into a new order
mainly means most of the word, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A charming fair-haired person arranges a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the E of BLONDE; 'organised' rearranges WINSOME and BLOND. 'trip' means a drug experience, not a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to be overwhelmed or to experience something mind-bending, which a drug trip is an example of.

clue.text: Introduction to open country noise

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or open grassland
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: An opening passage on rural sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a preamble or opening segment leading into the main part.

clue.text: Backbone of Green support in Europe? On the contrary

indicators.note: the clue says support in Europe; on the contrary puts the abbreviation first, then the garment

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry
a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A question about the mainstay of the Green Party's backing across the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' reverses the stated order of the last two pieces, so Europe precedes support.
explanation.definitionFit: Part for whole: one of the bones making up the spine, which here stands for it.

clue.text: Make light of vocalise not about two notes in it

indicators.note: two notes go in it, inside the shortened word
not says the following piece is removed from the word

parts.note: CA, circa, means about
la and ti are notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Mock a singing exercise that lacks a couple of notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make light' suggests mockery, but it is the chemist's sense. 'not about' strips circa's abbreviation to leave VOLISE, and 'in it' houses the sol-fa pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical sense: to turn a liquid or solid into vapour, making it as weightless as gas.

clue.text: Take in pan to festival in centre of Cracow for obsessive employee?

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: a wok is a Chinese frying pan
R, from Latin recipe, is the prescription abbreviation for take

indicators.note: the festival sits in the middle letters, between them
the centre of the city name is its middle two letters

parts.note: Holi is the Hindu spring festival of colours

explanation.surface: Someone travels with a pan to a festival in a Polish city.
explanation.walkthrough: Take as R is the prescription convention (Latin recipe). The question mark flags that the definition is playful: a compulsive worker, not literally an employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone addicted to labour, who cannot stop toiling: a compulsive worker.

clue.text: River of reported repute

indicators.note: what is reported is spoken, so the sound of the word is what counts

parts.note: odour means reputation, as in being in good or bad odour

explanation.surface: A river said to have a reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a major river forming much of the border between Germany and Poland.

clue.text: In Kent perhaps, Norm dined apart

parts.note: Kent is a county in the south-east of England, SE for short
par is the norm or standard
to dine is to eat; dined is ate

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Kent, a man called Norm ate alone.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in South East England; 'Norm' looks like a man's name but means the standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: set or kept away from each other, not together.

clue.text: Finished cut below

indicators.note: cut here trims letters from both ends of the word

parts.note: beneath means below

explanation.surface: A garment was completed and trimmed below.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' takes BE off the front and H off the end of BENEATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tidily done, well finished with clean lines.

clue.text: A minute type of heather found in the country

parts.note: Erica is the botanical genus of heather

explanation.surface: A tiny variety of heather grows in this nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the land of the United States, often called this for short.

clue.text: Gradually diminish dubious credo and account for it magnetically

parts.note: to taper is to narrow or lessen bit by bit

indicators.note: a dubious version is unreliable, so the letters of the creed are muddled

explanation.surface: Slowly abandon a questionable belief and explain it with your charm.
explanation.definitionFit: To register sound on a magnetic strip of the kind used in cassettes and reel machines.

clue.text: Eloquent person in church mostly

indicators.note: mostly keeps most of the word, dropping its final letter

parts.note: an oratory is a small chapel or church

explanation.surface: A fine speaker is usually found in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a skilled public speaker who moves audiences.

clue.text: On beginning of action turn over smoothly

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

indicators.note: the beginning of the word is its first letter

parts.note: T/O, TO, is short for turnover

explanation.surface: As soon as things start, someone rolls over without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the on side is also known as the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical direction: notes played in a flowing, connected way without breaks.

clue.text: Cast off sin? Not her

parts.note: to shed is to cast off, as a snake its skin
evil is sin, wickedness

explanation.surface: Would this woman ever renounce wrongdoing? Certainly not.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a wicked woman is the last person to cast off sin.
explanation.definitionFit: A malicious, cruel woman who would never abandon wickedness.

clue.text: Note about a distant expedition

indicators.note: one piece about another goes round it

parts.note: si is an older name for the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
distant means far

explanation.surface: A message concerning a faraway trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an overland journey, especially in Africa, to see or hunt wildlife.

clue.text: Grumble about insect that's loud

parts.note: a bee is an insect
F, forte, is the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a noisy buzzing insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a complaint or gripe.

clue.text: I am the answer to your prayers, existing to have time for learner's copying

parts.note: contracted, I am is I'm
the very thing you wanted is it, as in 'this is it'

indicators.note: to have one letter for another is to swap it in
time goes in for, in place of, the learner's letter

parts.note: existing means alive
L is the learner sign on British cars

explanation.surface: A boastful claim to be the perfect answer, followed by a learner copying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have time for learner's' swaps the L in ALIVE for T, giving ATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: mimicking or modelled on something else.

clue.text: In a frenzy in the morning's all right

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Someone is frantic early on, yet insists everything is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: running wild, out of control in a violent rage.

clue.text: Lizard's taken Ecstasy to measure delay

indicators.note: the lizard's taken the drug in, holding it inside

parts.note: the Komodo dragon is a lizard; the possessive gives the S
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
feet are a unit of measure

explanation.surface: A reptile on drugs tries to gauge a hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken' puts E inside DRAGONS, before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to be deliberately slow, putting off doing something.
